draft.title: ATP and energy
card: ATP (adenosine triphosphate) is the molecule that gives muscles the energy to contract. When ATP is broken down, it releases energy and the muscle can use it.
The body stores only a small amount of ATP in the muscles. This is enough for just a few seconds of movement.
To keep moving, the body must keep remaking ATP from the food we eat. It does this through three energy systems.
The three systems are the ATP-PC system, the anaerobic glycolysis system and the aerobic system. Each one remakes ATP in a different way. They are covered in later points.
draft.remember: Muscles run on ATP, and the body must keep remaking it because it stores so little.

a.q: Why must the body keep remaking ATP during exercise?
opts: Only a small amount is stored in the muscles
Muscles can only use ATP once a day
ATP is stored in the blood and runs out there
The body makes ATP only after exercise ends
a.why: The muscles hold only a small store of ATP, so it is used up within seconds. The body must keep remaking it to keep moving. ATP is not kept in large amounts anywhere, so the idea that a big store sits in the blood is wrong.
a.clue: Think about how much ATP the muscles hold.

b.q: Jas jogs for 30 minutes at a steady pace. Which statement best explains how her muscles keep working?
opts: Her body keeps remaking ATP through its energy systems
Her muscles use the ATP they stored before the jog
Her muscles work without ATP after the first minute
Her body stops using ATP once she settles into a pace
b.why: The small ATP store would run out within seconds, so Jas's body must keep remaking ATP through the energy systems. Using only the stored ATP is tempting, but the store is far too small to last 30 minutes.
b.clue: Stored ATP lasts only a few seconds.

a.best: Only a small amount is stored in the muscles

b.best: Her body keeps remaking ATP through its energy systems
